q: 1. The contour interval is kept inversely proportional to ...............
options: time and expense of field work
steepness of the configuration of the area
explain: On steep ground, contours are close together, so a larger interval is used; on flat ground, a smaller interval is used to show detail.

q: 2. The suitable contour interval for a map with scale 1:10000 is ...............
explain: A common rule for contour interval is 25 / (number of cm per km). For 1:10000 (10 cm = 1 km), it would be 2.5m, so 2m is the closest standard interval.

q: 3. In direct method of contouring, the process of locating or identifying points lying on a contour called .............
explain: Vertical control is the process used to find points of the same elevation (the contour line) using a level and staff.

q: 4. From any point on the surface with a given inclination .............
options: only one contour gradient is possible
explain: From a single point, you can go in two directions along the hillside to maintain a specific gradient.

q: 5. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from .............
explain: Starting from a saddle or ridge allows the surveyor to work downwards and find the best alignment for a road gradient.
